announcements.title: Foundations for AI Problem Solving
announcements.author: Mesa School of Business
announcements.text:
Foundations for AI Problem Solving- Optional class
New to AI or curious about building products?
Drop in for a beginner-friendly introduction to AI and AI-powered product building.
What we’ll explore:
01. Spot the problem
How do you identify a real problem worth solving?
02. Think with AI
Where can AI actually help, and where does it not?
03. From idea to product
How do you turn a problem into a simple product concept?
04. Meet your AI co-builder
A quick introduction to tools like Claude and how they’re changing the way products are built.
05. See what’s possible
Walk through examples and leave with a clearer idea of what you can start building yourself.

announcements.title: Data Driven Decision Making: End Term Exam Guidelines
announcements.author: Mesa School of Business
announcements.text:
Dear Mavericks,
As we approach the end of the term, here is what to expect in the Data Driven Decision Making end term exam.
Exam Format
• The exam is a 1.5-hour, in-class exam, similar in format to the Mid Term.

• You may bring a one-page sheet (1 pager) with formulas or concept references.

What the Exam Covers
The exam will test your ability to work with start-up data across six levels, L0 to L5. Levels L0 to L4 are Excel-based, and L5 is a theoretical Big Mastery Question.
• L0: Basic Data Aggregation and Data Cleaning

• L1: Lookups

• L2: Dashboard and Conditional Formatting

• L3: Pivots, Slicers and Conditional Formatting

• L4: Query and Export

• L5: Big Mastery Question

Please Note: What Is Not Allowed
• Late submissions will not be accepted.

• Using AI or any other tools for automated data analysis is not permitted.

• Submissions will be cross-checked against those of your classmates, and any signs of similarity will be flagged.

We encourage you to revisit your practice files and prepare your one-pager thoughtfully, as it will serve you best when it reflects your own understanding.
Best of luck with your preparation!

announcements.title: Entrepreneurship 101 Weekly Assignments
announcements.author: Mesa School of Business
announcements.text:
Hi Mavericks,
Following on what was discussed in Entrepreneurship 101, your Weekly assignment for Idea Lab Sprint is now live on Nexus.
What you need to do:
Download the weekly assignment document from Nexus.
Nexus>Courses>Entreprenuership 101>Assignments
• Fill in all sections in your own words based on the techniques covered in the class.

• Submit the completed Word file (.docx) on Nexus before the deadline.

A few important notes:
• Submissions are individual. If you're working on an idea with a co-founder from another section, each of you must complete and submit your own document with your own thinking. You can work on shared ideas, but make sure to submit individual submissions.

• Be specific and honest. The document asks for numbers, observed facts, and real conversations, not hypotheticals. If your research in Section 4 changes what you wrote in Section 1, don't erase it. 

• Reason: These weekly assignments are designed to build your ability to think clearly and rigorously about your idea - something you'll need for Mesa Startup Lab (MSL) and the Idea Lab Sprint (ILS). ILS is particularly relevant if you're still developing your idea or came in after MSL applications - it's a direct pathway to get structured support from the team on your concept.

There will assignments across the term, one after every two sessions, which will be updated on Nexus itself.
Reach out on Nexus if you have questions on the submission process.
Good luck
